hook_text: Wind it, wire it, test it three times. The magnet that passes is the one whose team wrote everything down.
clip_script: Making day. Nail first: hold it to a magnet, pull away, make sure it lets go of a clip. Tape the sharp ends. Now wind: tight, one way, counting in tens, fifty down, fifty back, same direction, one hundred. Strip the ends until the copper shines. Lay out the loop like the diagram: cell, switch, coil, bulb. Switch last. Press. The bulb lights, so the coil is live. Now the real test. Dip, lift, count the clips. Let go, count what still hangs after a second. Three times. Ten up and none left means it passes. Under ten? Change one thing: more turns, a second cell, check the direction. Clips hanging on? Softer nail. Write every number down. On the crane, the only magnet that counts is the one you can prove.
visual_style: Whiteboard nail with turns wrapping on; four symbols joining into a loop; a bulb lighting; clips leaping and dropping; a results table filling with three rows.
mood: Focused and hands-on, a bench coming to life.
pacing: Nail, wind, strip, loop, press, dip, count, fix, write, each a beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build the electromagnet that will hang from your crane.
